PER COURT :
. This is an appeal challenging the award passed by the reference Court i.e. Civil Judge Senior Division, Bhusawal dated 05th September, 2019, by which several land references were decided.

So far as present appeal is concerned, the relevant land reference would be in L.A.R. No. 528 of 2014 (Old L.A.R. No. 954 of 2007).
2.

Challenging the award passed by the reference Court, it is contended by learned counsel for the appellant/claimant that the sale-deeds, duly proved on record by the claimants, were not taken into consideration on the ground that those three sale-deeds were of village Ainpur and Khirdi, whereas the land acquired was from Bhamalwadi.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the aforesaid sale-deeds ought to have been taken into consideration since those two villages were adjacent to village Bhamalwadi.
According to him, the reference Court had awarded rate of Rs.4 per sq. mtr.

For open space of land and so far as the claimant is concerned, the open space was of 60 sq.
mtr.
He further submitted that in fact for arriving at the rate, the acquiring body should not have been relied upon only three sale-deeds, but several other materials should have been brought on record.
He submitted that the Court can take judicial note of the fact that in the sale-deed, normally less consideration is mentioned.

He submitted that the act of not producing best material in the form of evidence before the 903-FA-400-20.odt reference Court at the instance of acquiring body is deliberate act and what is required to be considered is the highest sale instance.

According to him,
thus the amount of Rs.4 per sq. mtr. is meager and ought to have been increased in the light of the various sale instances produced on record.

3. In order to buttress is contention, he has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Mahesh Dattatray Thirthkar Vs. State of Maharashtra, reported in AIR 2009 SC 2238, more particularly paragraph nos. 27, 29, 30 and 32, wherein the Apex Court has held that burden of proving the true market value of acquired property is on the State that has acquired it for a particular purpose.

sentences.text: The Court has also observed that where the landowner has been able to show, by the testimony and valuation report of the expert valuer, that the award of compensation passed by the Land Acquisition Officer was inadequate, the onus shifts on the State to adduce sufficient evidence to sustain the award.

4. He has also relied upon the judgment reported in 2008 (3) AIR Bom R 632 in Executive Engineer,
P.W.D. VI (R & B)m Margaon and Anr. Vs. Versus Antonion Almeida and Ors., more particularly paragraph nos. 11 and 12, wherein this Court has stated that for determination of market value,
comparable sale instances are required to be taken into consideration and if there are dissimilarities in regard to locality, shape, size or nature between 903-FA-400-20.odt land covered by sales and land acquired

6.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the acquiring body has submitted that the reference Court has taken into consideration various aspects, and therefore, intervention at the hands of this Court is not required.
7. I have thoughtfully considered the argument advanced by both the counsels so also have gone through the various case laws cited at the bar.

8. In the present case, the notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act was issued on 28th February, 2002, whereas the Special Land Acquisition Officer has passed the award on 28 th January, 2005.
The land of the appellant, more particularly, House No.72 and 60 sq.mtr. open space was 903-FA-400-20.odt awarded Rs.200/- sq.mtr. by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
After filing of reference, the reference Court had enhanced compensation for open land to the rate of Rs.400/- sq.mtr.
The land acquired was situated in village Bhamalwadi, Tq. Raver and it was acquired for construction of pond / reservoir.

9. At this juncture it is necessary to mention here that the reference Court while enhancing compensation from Rs.200/- to Rs400/- sq.mtr. has taken into consideration four sale-deeds produced on record by the acquiring body which were of village Bhamalwadi only.

It is further necessary to mention here that out of four sale-deeds, the highest sale-deed was showing that the sale consideration was of Rs.218/- per sq.mtr. and thereafter by adopting the method of guess work,
the compensation was enhanced from Rs.200/- to Rs.400/- sq.mtr.
Thus the findings given by the reference Court are based on the best material produced by the acquiring body.
10. At this stage it is necessary to mention here that what was produced by the claimant as sale instances were three sale-deeds, one of village Ainpur and two of village Khirdi.
The reference Court has not taken into consideration the said sale instances by giving a finding that village Khirdi and Ainpur are bigger than village Bhamalwadi.

The reference Court thereafter adopted the guess formula and granted compensation of Rs.400/-
903-FA-400-20.odt sq.mtr.

In this regard it is necessary to reproduce the finding given by the reference Court at paragraph no. 11, which reads thus :-
"11.
In above references it has been observed that the house from two sale instances were adjoining to the road and the house of one of the sale instance was having terrace.
It is to be noted that the claimants have admitted that the village Khirdi and Ainpur are bigger than their village.

Therefore,
the sale instances are not taken as comparable one and fixed the rate of open land by guess work.
In the present reference the claimants have filed map to show that the village Khirdi and Ainpur are adjoining villages of Bhamalwadi.
But this map is not useful for the claimants because the village Khirdi and Ainpur are bigger than that of village Bhamalwadi.
Further the location of the house properties from the sale instances are difference altogether from the acquired house properties as discussed above.
Considering the similarity, the rate can be fixed on the basis of rule of parity.
The claimants have claimed the compensation for their open land.

There is no structure upon the open Sitaram Zendu Patil Thr Lrs ... vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer - 1 ... on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187146223/
3 land but still in evidence the claimants have tried to show the structure.

sentences.text: It appears that, due to similar matters, they deposed about it inadvertently."

11. So far as sale-deeds produced and which are discussed in paragraph no.9 of the reference Court judgment are concerned, suffice it to say that those sale-deeds were of the lands on which structure was also standing.
The reference Court has taken into consideration that villages Khirdi and Ainpur were the bigger villages, and therefore, proper method which was adopted was guess work.
The findings further show that the map was also submitted for consideration, but same was ignored by the advancing reason that both the villages were bigger than village Bhamalwadi.
Nothing has been brought on record to show that the findings given by the reference Court are illegal or perverse.
So far as the sale instances produced by the claimant are concerned, it is already stated that it pertains to the standing structure also.
In that view of the matter, parity cannot be claimed by the claimant.
13. As far as the judgments cited supra and the law laid down by various Courts cannot be disputed at all, suffice it to say every case will differ on its own fact.
It is for the claimant to produce best material before the reference Court to arrive at a conclusion that the claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation.
This Court cannot draw inference that normally less price is mentioned in the sale-deed, in absence of any material.
In that view of the matter, I am of the opinion that no interference is required in the impugned judgment and award.
Accordingly appeal is dismissed.
